item.title: Aesthetics for the Maimed
item.description: An intentionally severe essay proposing “liberal gothic” as a bounded label for cultural forms organized around haunted interiority, therapeutic recognition, damaged intimacy, and moralized injury, while testing—and sharply limiting—the stronger claim that contemporary culture deliberately preserves suffering for profit.

item.title: Dead Symbols and their Worship
item.description: An intentionally severe, aphoristic essay arguing that parts of mathematical culture confuse abstraction, difficulty, and proximity to unsolved problems with intellectual strength, while undervaluing synthesis, closure, pedagogy, and completed mastery.

item.title: The Emptiness of Deleuze
item.description: Tests a polemical critique of Deleuze and finds that the strongest inherited charges misstate his ontology, while a narrower criticism survives: Deleuzian concepts explain genesis, transformation, and capture more readily than they supply normative criteria or institutional designs for legitimate durable political order.
